Title: Turn your Mac Mini into a vintage desktop with the M5 Retro Dock Station | High-Tech Mag
# Turn your Mac Mini into a vintage desktop with the M5 Retro Dock Station. A small accessory blends nostalgic design with practical upgrades for Mac Mini users, including a 5-inch display and NVMe slot. * What the M5 Retro Dock adds to your setup. Retro styling has become a popular way to personalize modern hardware, and the **M5 Retro Dock Station** from **Wokyis** is one of the latest examples. Retailing on **Amazon** for **$169.99**, this dock is designed to sit on top of an **M4 Mac Mini** and to connect via the Mini’s **USB-C** port. Rather than an elaborate case swap, the dock attaches quickly and adds two immediately visible upgrades: a tiny integrated screen and an internal expansion bay for solid-state storage. The dock’s 5-inch panel provides a small, dedicated surface for glanceable information, while its **M.2 NVMe** slot accommodates a high-speed SSD to increase the Mac Mini’s internal capacity. The rest of this piece breaks down what the dock delivers, why it matters in the current market, and whether it’s worth adding to your desk setup. The dock installs directly on the top of your **M4 Mac Mini** and links through the Mini’s **USB-C** connection, creating a compact retro silhouette while preserving the computer’s original casing. Arguably the most practical feature is the dock’s integrated **M.2 NVMe** slot, which allows owners to install one of the market’s faster consumer **SSDs** and expand storage without opening the Mac Mini. For users who already own a Mac Mini, accessories like the **M5 Retro Dock Station** offer both a visible personalization and a pragmatic storage option while the broader market catches up. Unlike the DIY route of transplanting a Mac Mini’s board into a vintage iMac shell—a process that can be time-consuming and risky—the M5 dock installs within minutes and without opening the Mini. If your priorities are aesthetic flair and affordable storage expansion, the **M5 Retro Dock Station** provides a compact way to achieve both. It won’t replace primary displays or internal upgrades performed by professionals, but it does offer a quick, reversible mod that adds a **5-inch 720p** display and an **M.2 NVMe** expansion slot for *SSD* upgrades.
